events.notes: Fires early and at most once or twice per save: attractionCount only climbs, so the trigger closes for good at the second attraction. A deliberately low-severity opener. Prose says ATTRACTIVENESS and park entertainment and never tourism, because the palette has no tourism modifier. Two conventions applied to every event in this file. (1) Pressures are SALIENCE, not credit (owner ruling, wave 3): all three point the same way on the axis and differ only in magnitude, success quieter and failure louder. Government credit and blame are derived by the engine from the slot outcome and tier, never authored here. (2) No effect id appears in both activeEffects and successEffects: the palette carries no sign and all three story scales are positive, so that shape would reapply the same modifier at twice the magnitude and call it a reward.
events.name: Nothing To Put On A Postcard
events.description: The city has almost nothing worth a detour. Visitors pass through on the way somewhere else, the local paper reprints the same three photographs every summer, and a council motion asks aloud what exactly the place is for.
events.ignoreText: Let the city speak for itself. Somewhere to live does not have to be somewhere to visit.
events.goalText: Get something built worth crossing town for, and have it standing before the next review.
events.powerOverrideText: Declare the question closed and instruct officers to stop briefing against the skyline.
events.successText: There is somewhere to take people now, and the city's attractiveness has caught up with its ambitions.
events.failText: Another year, still nothing. Confidence in the administration's feel for the place has slipped.

events.notes: Congestion at 0.45 of the calibrated flow reference is an ordinary mid-game reading, so expect this a few times a decade in a car-dependent city and rarely in a transit-led one. The check only asks that congestion did not get worse over the ONE month the story is actually alive — a story opens at M and resolves at M+1, so cycleMonths is the cadence and not the window the player owns. A zero threshold rescales cleanly from the two-month window an earlier draft used: 'no worse' means the same thing over either span.
events.name: The Lane That Started A Fight
events.description: A proposal to take a traffic lane for bicycles has turned two streets into a proxy war over what the roads are for. Shopkeepers want the parking, cycling groups want the lane, and the traffic is bad enough that both sides think the numbers prove them right.
events.ignoreText: Let the two sides shout it out. The lane markings can wait for a quieter year.
events.goalText: Push the scheme through and hold congestion no worse than it is today.
events.powerOverrideText: Paint the lane overnight and take the complaints personally.
events.successText: The lane is in, more people are riding, and the junctions are calmer than the objectors predicted.
events.failText: The scheme stalled, the traffic did not, and households have gone back to keeping a car for every trip.

events.notes: A third of a district's residents with no schooling at all is common wherever housing has outrun the school network — most cities will see this once or twice before the second elementary school lands. Trigger and check are exact complements at 0.32, so there is no band in which a district can fail the check while being invisible in the trigger: anyDistrict at or above, allDistricts below.
events.name: The Waiting List
events.description: One part of town has more children than places to put them. The register runs to three pages, families are being told to try the district across the river, and the head teacher has stopped answering the phone.
events.ignoreText: The register will shorten on its own as the birth cohort passes through. Nothing needs building.
events.goalText: Get schooling to the district that has none, and clear the shortfall everywhere before the review.
events.powerOverrideText: Overrule the catchment objections and open places wherever they will fit.
events.successText: The places exist. Progression to college has picked up and the university is fielding enquiries it never used to get.
events.failText: The list is longer than it was. A cohort has been written off, and the offending that follows an idle one has started to show.

events.notes: RE-READ AGAINST THE REAL RANGE. serviceCoverage is the mean of NINE channels with garbage, transit, water and electricity hard-zeroed, so it tops out at 5/9 = 0.5556 and never approaches 1.0 (CivicEventCatalogLoader.AttainableMaximum). An earlier draft used 0.35 on a 0-1 assumption; that is 63% of everything attainable, which would have made this the permanent state of most cities rather than a story. Lowered to 0.30 — 54% of the ceiling, meaning the five live channels average about 54% coverage — which is a district genuinely behind rather than a district merely imperfect. Expect it every few years in a growing city and almost never in a mature one. Exact complements at 0.30, and deliberately the same number glob-service-desert's district floor is measured against, so the mandatory event is a legible strict subset: this one needs ONE district below the line, that one needs every district below it. Clears on allDistricts, so annexing a fresh unserviced district re-opens it — the intended reading.
events.name: Four Hours In A Corridor
events.description: One district's services have fallen far enough behind its population that the wait is measured in corridors rather than minutes. The neighbouring districts are coping; this one has stopped pretending to.
events.ignoreText: Coverage will follow the buildings eventually. Tell people to use the facilities one district over.
events.goalText: Lift every district's service coverage clear of the line before the next review.
events.powerOverrideText: Reassign capacity from the comfortable districts and dare them to complain.
events.successText: Coverage is level across the city again and the hospitals are getting more out of what they have.
events.failText: The queue outlasted the promise, and the untreated cases have started to show up in the health figures.

events.notes: Thirty-two minutes sits at the top of the engine's own 'long' commute band (25-40) and the bottom of 'punishing', so it is reachable in any city that has let housing and jobs drift apart. Expect it perhaps twice a decade. Trigger and check are exact complements: getting back under the line is the whole ask, with no gap the player is scored on but never told about. City scope only — commuteMinutes has no district reading.
events.name: The Hour Each Way
events.description: The average one-way journey to work has crossed the line where people stop calling it a commute and start calling it a second job. Nobody blames a single road; everybody blames the council.
events.ignoreText: People chose where to live. The council is not a taxi service.
events.goalText: Bring the average journey back below the line by the next review.
events.powerOverrideText: Force the timetable and junction changes through without consultation.
events.successText: Journeys are shorter, the main roads are safer, and enough people have taken to bikes to be visible on them.
events.failText: The journey got longer. Fares have risen for those who gave up and now book a taxi, and everyone else keeps a car for everything.

events.notes: CONFIRMED AGAINST THE REAL RANGE, and unchanged. pollution tops out at 0.75 rather than 1.0, because water is hard-zeroed in the mean of four (CivicEventCatalogLoader.AttainableMaximum). 0.28 is therefore 37% of attainable — the three live channels averaging about 0.37 — which means industry or landfill sitting on top of housing: uncommon but entirely reachable, perhaps once a decade in a city with heavy industry and never in one without. Severity 4 rather than 5: the city can still function around it. Trigger and check are exact complements at 0.28; an earlier draft checked 0.24 and so scored the player against districts sitting in the 0.24-0.28 band that the trigger never mentioned. The negative growth pressure is deliberate and identical in direction across all three outcomes: a contamination story is where the pro-development pole LOSES ground, and under the salience ruling that direction must not flip between outcomes.
events.name: What Is Under The Playing Field
events.description: Soil taken from a district's open ground came back dirty enough that the samples were run twice. Residents have worked out which streets are involved faster than the notification letters could reach them.
events.ignoreText: Publish the readings, fence the worst corner, and let the ground recover on its own timetable.
events.goalText: Bring every district's pollution back under the line before the next review.
events.powerOverrideText: Seize the site, halt the works, and settle the arguments afterwards.
events.successText: The readings have come down city-wide, and the industrial estates are running cleaner without running slower.
events.failText: The contamination spread and the health figures followed it. Nobody in that district believes a council letter now.

events.notes: One of the two severity-5 events, and it should feel like one: the city crime statistic is normalised against a reference max of 100, so 0.55 means over half the reference rate city-wide, which takes sustained neglect of policing rather than one bad district. Expect it once in a save, if ever. Trigger and check are exact complements, so simply getting back under the line clears it.
events.name: The City Stops Reporting It
events.description: Crime across the whole city has reached the point where residents have stopped calling it in, which is the only reason the figures are not worse. Insurers have started writing the city into their premiums by name.
events.ignoreText: Say nothing and hope the figures turn. There is no budget for a police expansion this year.
events.goalText: Get the city crime rate back below the line and keep it there to the review.
events.powerOverrideText: Declare an emergency policing posture and answer to the inquiry later.
events.successText: Response times are down, monitoring is catching what it used to miss, and the figures have turned for the first time in years.
events.failText: It got worse. Crime is now something residents plan around rather than report, and everyone knows who let it get there.

events.notes: The district reading is derived from buildings' own crime producers rather than the city statistic, so one badly served block reaches 0.40 long before the city average does. Expect this several times over a long save — it is the ordinary, recurring version of the city-wide crime event and is priced at severity 3 accordingly. Trigger and check are exact complements at 0.40; an earlier draft checked 0.35, which would have failed the player over a district sitting quietly in the 0.35-0.40 band that the story never named.
events.name: The Streets Everyone Names
events.description: One district has become the answer to the question of where not to go after dark. The rest of the city is fine, which is exactly what residents there find hardest to hear.
events.ignoreText: It is one district. Policing it harder than everywhere else would make the resentment worse.
events.goalText: Bring every district below the line, not just the ones already there.
events.powerOverrideText: Flood the district with patrols and let the civil liberties argument happen afterwards.
events.successText: Response times in the district match the rest of the city, monitoring has caught up, and the blackspot has closed.
events.failText: The reputation has hardened and the offending has spread with it. The district has stopped expecting help.

events.notes: Under five per cent of residents at the top education tier is the default state of any city without a university, so this fires reliably in the first decades and closes once higher education is established. The check is RELATIVE TO BASELINE with a small positive threshold rather than an absolute level, and that is what makes it winnable from the state the trigger describes: an earlier draft asked for an absolute 0.06, which a city with no campus could not reach inside a cycle whatever the player did — the notes conceded as much, which is how the contradiction was caught. Two tenths of a point above the reading taken when the story opened is movable by building the campus, and marginally by in-migration even without one. City scope, as a relative check must be.
events.name: They Come Back For Christmas
events.description: The city's brightest school leavers study elsewhere and stay elsewhere. Employers advertise into a market that empties every September, and the graduate share of the population has stopped climbing.
events.ignoreText: Cities that need graduates attract graduates. Subsidising the ones who leave is money after the fact.
events.goalText: Move the graduate share upward from where it stands today, and have it showing by the review.
events.powerOverrideText: Fund the campus places directly and account for it later.
events.successText: Enrolment is up and graduations with it, from the colleges and the university alike. The share is climbing again.
events.failText: Another cohort has gone. Offices are running short of the skills they advertise for, and the city is paying for it.

events.notes: Congestion at 0.60 of the calibrated flow reference is a genuinely jammed city rather than a busy one — reachable, but only after the road network has been left behind by growth for years. Perhaps once a decade. The check asks for a measurable fall rather than an absolute level, so it stays winnable in a very large city where an absolute target would not be. RE-DERIVED FOR THE ONE-MONTH STORY LIFE: an earlier draft asked for three points over two months, which charged the player for the month before they saw the card. Halved to 1.5 points over the single month a story actually lives, so the rate demanded is unchanged and only the span the player is answerable for has shrunk.
events.name: Gridlock
events.description: The network has stopped absorbing its own peaks. A single blocked junction now backs up across three districts, emergency vehicles are being routed the long way round, and the radio traffic report has become a standing joke.
events.ignoreText: Ride it out. Every growing city goes through a bad few years of traffic.
events.goalText: Get congestion measurably down before the review, not merely stabilised.
events.powerOverrideText: Impose the junction closures and speed changes by order, consultation cancelled.
events.successText: The network is breathing again. Traffic on the main roads is moving and the streets are safer for it.
events.failText: It seized further. Taxi fares have climbed, more households have gone back to driving everything, and nothing the council said held.

events.notes: Happiness reads 0-100, and a six-point fall over half a year is the signature of a tax rise, a service failure or a rent shock rather than ordinary noise — expect it a handful of times across a long save. RE-DERIVED FOR THE ONE-MONTH STORY LIFE: an earlier draft asked for a full point over two months. Halved to half a point over the single month a story lives, so the recovery rate demanded is unchanged. Deliberately modest either way: this is a mood, not a metric the player controls directly.
events.name: The Mood Has Turned
events.description: Nothing single has gone wrong, and everything has got slightly worse. Six months of small disappointments have added up to a city that has stopped giving the administration the benefit of the doubt.
events.ignoreText: Moods pass. Chasing a satisfaction figure with public money is how cities end up broke and still unhappy.
events.goalText: Turn the figure around — any measurable recovery by the next review.
events.powerOverrideText: Announce the recovery whether or not the figures agree, and dare anyone to check.
events.successText: The mood has lifted. There is more going on in the city than there was, and people have noticed.
events.failText: It kept sliding. The city is visibly less content than it was and less appealing to anyone considering it.

events.notes: homelessShare is a 0-1 share and real homelessness lives in the bottom couple of per cent, so two per cent is a visible crisis. Expect this whenever rents outrun incomes — perhaps two or three times across a long save. Trigger and check are exact complements: getting back under the line is the ask, rather than the halving an earlier draft demanded, which was a second and unstated bar on top of it. The council cannot set rents or build houses through the effect palette, so the prose promises shelter and support and never new homes.
events.name: Sleeping Rough
events.description: Two households in every hundred have nowhere of their own. It is no longer confined to one district or one doorway, and the first count anyone believes has just been published.
events.ignoreText: Move the tents on and say nothing. The figure will fall when the housing market turns.
events.goalText: Get the share of residents with nowhere to live back below the line before the next review.
events.powerOverrideText: Requisition what shelter can be found and answer the legal questions afterwards.
events.successText: The count is back under the line. People are indoors and supported, and the city is a calmer place for it.
events.failText: The count rose. Rough sleeping has become permanent, and the crime figures around it have moved with it.

events.notes: Forty-five per cent of residents in the low wealth tier is common in an industrial city and rare in a service one, so this fires reliably in some saves and never in others — the intended variation. Trigger and check are exact complements. Framed around trade cost and commercial tax because farm output is not reachable from the palette. city-import-cost sits in successEffects and NOT in activeEffects on purpose: the goal text names bringing goods in cheaper, so the lever the goal names has to be the one the success path actually pulls. An earlier draft had it in active and failure only, so the success route never touched it.
events.name: Everything Arrives By Lorry
events.description: The city buys in what it cannot make, and the households least able to absorb it are the ones paying for the haulage. Almost half of residents are now in the lowest wealth band, and the shelf prices explain most of it.
events.ignoreText: Prices are prices. Leaning on the traders would only move the cost somewhere less visible.
events.goalText: Cut what the city pays to bring goods in, and get households back out of the bottom wealth band.
events.powerOverrideText: Renegotiate the freight terms by decree and let the hauliers take it to arbitration.
events.successText: The cost of bringing goods in has come down, local commerce has been given room to breathe, and household budgets have followed.
events.failText: Sending goods out and buying services in both cost more than they did. The squeeze on the poorest households has tightened.

events.notes: A three-point rise in the city pollution mean over six months is what a new industrial estate looks like in the figures — 4% of the 0.75 the metric can actually reach, so a real move rather than a rounding artefact — so this tracks the player's own building rather than a fixed level — expect it whenever industry expands, which in most saves is several times. The check merely asks that the rise stopped over the one month the story lives, which is fair for something the player has just deliberately built; a zero threshold rescales cleanly from the two-month window an earlier draft used, since 'no worse' means the same over either span. city-industrial-air-pollution now appears in successEffects only: an earlier draft had it in activeEffects too, which would have reapplied the same modifier at resolution while the success prose claimed the estates were running cleaner. The growth pressure is negative in all three outcomes and never flipped — an air-quality inquiry is where the pro-development pole loses ground whichever way it ends.
events.name: The Inquiry Nobody Called For
events.description: Air readings have climbed steadily for half a year and a councillor has read the series into the record. The industry that caused it is the same industry that paid for last year's budget, and everyone in the chamber knows it.
events.ignoreText: Let the inquiry report in its own time. The estates are what keep the city working.
events.goalText: Stop the rise. The readings must be no worse at the next review than they are now.
events.powerOverrideText: Close the inquiry down and instruct the monitoring team to report annually instead.
events.successText: The climb has stopped and the estates are producing more per unit of dirt than they were.
events.failText: The readings kept rising, the industrial waste with them, and the health cost is now in the record too.

events.notes: CORRECTED FREQUENCY CLAIM: an earlier draft said this fires once per save, which was wrong. milestoneLevel is monotonic and reuseCooldownMonths is 6, so once the city passes milestone 6 this re-pools every six months for the rest of the save. That is acceptable for a recurring negotiation and is why it is severity 2 and cheap, but it is a standing pool member rather than a one-off, and wave 7 should know that when it balances the pool mix. The check is now RELATIVE TO BASELINE — one point of happiness above the reading taken when the talks opened — rather than the absolute 62 an earlier draft used, which was decided at draft time: a city at 70 passed for free and a city at 50 could not reach it however well it negotiated.
events.name: The Terms Come Up For Renewal
events.description: The city has grown into the bracket where lenders take an interest in how it is run. The terms on its borrowing are up for review, the running costs of the city's own buildings are being held flat while the talks last, and the case rests less on the accounts than on whether the city looks like a going concern.
events.ignoreText: Take whatever is offered. Haggling over a rate is not what the office is for.
events.goalText: Have the city measurably more contented at the review than when the talks opened, and argue for better terms on the strength of it.
events.powerOverrideText: Sign the terms unread and present them to the chamber as settled.
events.successText: Better terms secured. The city's borrowing costs less than it did when the talks opened.
events.failText: The terms hardened. Borrowing is dearer and the services the city buys in cost more than they did.

events.notes: More than half a district in the lowest wealth band happens wherever cheap housing clusters, which in practice is most cities with more than a handful of districts — expect it every few years. Exact complements at 0.55. The allDistricts check makes it about levelling the worst block rather than about the city average, which is what makes the same month read differently block to block.
events.name: The Cheap Side Of The River
events.description: One district has quietly become where you live when you cannot afford anywhere else. Over half its households are in the lowest wealth band, the shops that survive are the ones that sell on credit, and nobody in the chamber represents it.
events.ignoreText: Every city has a cheap district. Interfering with it would only price out the people it shelters.
events.goalText: Lift the district, and have no district left above the line by the next review.
events.powerOverrideText: Direct the relief where you judge it needed and skip the consultation.
events.successText: Local commerce there has been given room on its tax, the shops that were closing are trading again, and the gap between the two sides of the city has narrowed.
events.failText: The gap widened. Buildings there cost more to keep standing than they earn, and the crime figures have moved accordingly.

events.notes: A five-point fall in the middle wealth share across a year is a real move rather than noise — the wealth mix drifts by that much whenever taxes, rents or the job mix change materially, so expect this a few times across a long save. The check only asks that the slide stopped over the one month a story lives, which keeps it winnable without engineering the whole economy; the zero threshold rescales cleanly from the two-month window an earlier draft used.
events.name: The Middle Gives Way
events.description: The city has not got poorer so much as hollowed out. A year of small pressures has moved households out of the middle band in both directions, and the people who used to be the reliable vote no longer feel reliably anything.
events.ignoreText: Wealth bands move. Reading a political crisis into a demographic drift is how administrations waste a term.
events.goalText: Stop the slide. The middle band must be no smaller at the review than it is now.
events.powerOverrideText: Declare the figures a statistical artefact and instruct the office to stop publishing the series.
events.successText: The slide has stopped. Local commerce is lighter on tax and households have felt the difference.
events.failText: It kept going. Imports and the city's own running costs both climbed, and the squeeze has become the story of the term.

events.notes: Deliberately the easiest trigger in the file — congestion at 0.35 is an ordinary busy city — and priced at severity 1 to match. It is here to give the pool a supply of small, cheap stories so that the mandatory tier stays rare by contrast. Expect it often in any car-dependent city. The check reads one month, the life of a story, and its zero threshold rescales cleanly from the two-month window an earlier draft used. district-parking-fee moved out of activeEffects so that success is not the same modifier applied twice.
events.name: The Parking Charge Nobody Voted For
events.description: A revised parking tariff has produced more correspondence than the last three budgets combined. The traffic is bad enough to justify it and the letters are angry enough to make that irrelevant.
events.ignoreText: Freeze the tariff and let the traffic sort itself out. It is not worth the postbag.
events.goalText: Hold the charge, and hold congestion no worse than it is now.
events.powerOverrideText: Sign the tariff off over the objections and stop replying to the letters.
events.successText: The charge stuck, the kerbside turns over properly again, and more short trips are being made on two wheels.
events.failText: The charge was pulled. More households are keeping a car standing ready and the streets show it.

events.notes: PROVISIONAL THRESHOLDS, pending the AGORA-STATCOLLECTION census. citizensMovedAway is census-gated — its units are unresolved, so it is authored as a delta, which survives the ambiguity in direction. BOTH HALVES ARE NOW AUTHORED AGAINST ONE STATED READING: cumulative since founding, under which the trigger means four hundred departures in half a year — a running rate of about sixty-seven a month — and the check means fewer than fifty over the one month the story lives, so roughly three quarters of the rate that opened it. An earlier draft checked 'delta <= 0', which under that same reading demanded literally zero departures in a city already losing four hundred every six months — unachievable, so failText printed at every resolution. RE-DERIVED FOR THE ONE-MONTH STORY LIFE: the draft after that asked for fewer than a hundred over two months, which is the same rate but charged the player for the month before they saw the card. The reading cannot be settled from refsrc: m_CollectionType is a field on StatisticsPrefab/StatisticsData, which is authored asset data, and refsrc holds decompiled C# only. That is precisely why wave 1 specified a runtime census. Wave 7 owns both numbers.
events.name: The Vans Going The Other Way
events.description: Removal vans have been leaving faster than they arrive for half a year now. The city has not shrunk yet, but the trend has been read into the record and there is no comfortable explanation for it.
events.ignoreText: People move. Chasing them with public money would be an admission the city cannot hold its own.
events.goalText: Slow the outflow to something the city can absorb before the next review.
events.powerOverrideText: Announce that the figures are seasonal and instruct the office to say so too.
events.successText: The outflow has slowed to a trickle. There is more to stay for than there was, and the city is a more appealing prospect for it.
events.failText: They kept leaving. The city is paying to run buildings for a population that is no longer there.

events.notes: uncollectedGarbage is the backlog SITTING AT PRODUCERS — not the infoview's stored garbage and not a landfill figure, and the prose says 'uncollected' throughout for that reason. Expect this whenever collection capacity falls behind a growing district, a few times per save. THE CHECK WAS RE-AIMED: it is a stock that oscillates with the collection rounds, so an earlier draft asking every district to post a non-positive two-month delta simultaneously was roughly p^N — on six districts a lottery rather than a goal. It is now one city-wide reading relative to the month the story opened: a single draw, and the aggregate is far smoother than any one district's saw-tooth. City scope, as a relative check must be. Least confident threshold in this file: the trigger's 2000 is a raw count in game units with no documented ceiling, and it goes to wave 7 as a calibration item at the same order of magnitude lane 3b now uses.
events.name: It Has Not Been Collected Since March
events.description: One district's refuse is piling up at the buildings that produce it faster than anything comes to take it away. The smell arrived first, the correspondence second, and the photographs third.
events.ignoreText: The rounds will catch up. Buying more trucks for one district sets a precedent the whole city will want.
events.goalText: Clear it. The city's uncollected refuse must be no higher at the review than it is today.
events.powerOverrideText: Commandeer whatever will carry refuse and worry about the contracts afterwards.
events.successText: The rounds are back on schedule, the uncollected piles are down across the city, and it is a cleaner place to walk through.
events.failText: It kept piling up. The health figures have started to move and the district has photographs of every week it was ignored.

events.notes: THE CHECK WAS RE-AIMED, and this is the important repair. Rent is unmodifiable — no id in the palette moves it — so an earlier draft that scored the player on holding rents flat demanded an outcome with zero levers: Goal was unwinnable and PowerOverride, which resolves Met automatically, was the only clearable route. The trigger still reads rent, because rent is what the story is ABOUT; the check now reads city happiness across the one month the story lives, which is what the council can actually move through tax relief and commercial rates. Its zero threshold rescales cleanly from the two-month window an earlier draft used. Goal, levers and success prose now all say the same thing: the council cannot cut a rent, only the weight of everything around it. Second-least confident threshold in the file — rent is in game currency with no documented ceiling, so the trigger's 120 over twelve months is an estimate of 'a district gentrifying noticeably' and goes to wave 7 with the garbage figure.
events.name: The Renewal Letter
events.description: Rents in one district have moved far enough in a year that the renewal letters are being opened in front of witnesses. The households leaving are not being replaced by the ones the district was built for.
events.ignoreText: The council does not set rents and should not pretend it can. Say so plainly and move on.
events.goalText: The council cannot touch the rent. Take the weight off everything around it and stop the city's mood falling any further.
events.powerOverrideText: Announce a freeze the city has no power to enforce and let the courts find out later.
events.successText: The slide stopped. The council could not cut a single rent, but it lightened everything else it touches, and households noticed.
events.failText: The mood fell with the letters. Imports and the city's own running costs climbed too, and households are being priced out of a district they built.

events.notes: An eight-point rise in the normalised crime rate over six months is what outgrowing your policing looks like, so this tends to arrive shortly before the city-wide crime wave and gives the player a chance to head it off. Expect it a few times per save. The check asks only that the rise stopped over the one month a story lives; its zero threshold rescales cleanly from the two-month window an earlier draft used. city-crime-response-time moved out of activeEffects: leaving it in both lists would have reapplied it at resolution while the success prose claimed response times had improved.
events.name: How Long It Takes Someone To Come
events.description: Crime has climbed steadily for six months and a leaked internal note puts the reason plainly: there are not enough officers to answer what is already being reported. The note was not meant to leave the building.
events.ignoreText: Dispute the note's methodology and let the figures settle. Recruitment takes longer than a news cycle anyway.
events.goalText: Halt the rise. Crime must be no higher at the review than it is today.
events.powerOverrideText: Suppress the note, reassign its author, and declare response times satisfactory.
events.successText: The rise has stopped. Officers are reaching calls faster and monitoring is picking up what used to be missed.
events.failText: It kept climbing. Offending has become routine in places it never was, and the leaked note reads like a prophecy.

events.notes: A normalised crime rate of 0.30 is an ordinary mid-game reading rather than a crisis, so this is the recurring, arguable version of the crime story and is priced at severity 2. Expect it several times per save. Exact complements. city-prison-time is SENTENCE LENGTH, not the cost of running a prison, and the prose says exactly that and nothing about budgets; it sits in successEffects only, so backing longer sentences is the reward path rather than a modifier applied twice.
events.name: How Long Is Long Enough
events.description: With crime a live issue rather than a crisis, the chamber has turned to sentencing. One side wants longer terms as a deterrent, the other says the city is arguing about the back end of a problem it has not addressed at the front.
events.ignoreText: Sentencing is not a council matter and saying so is the honest answer, however badly it goes down.
events.goalText: Back longer sentences and get the crime figures back below the line by the review.
events.powerOverrideText: Push the sentencing position through the chamber and let the dissenters vote against it on the record.
events.successText: Sentences are longer, monitoring is sharper, and the crime figures have come down enough to settle the argument for now.
events.failText: Crime kept climbing while the chamber argued about sentencing. It was the wrong end of the problem and everyone can see it.

events.notes: RE-READ AGAINST THE REAL RANGE. serviceCoverage tops out at 5/9 = 0.5556, not 1.0, because the sensor hard-zeroes garbage, transit, water and electricity (CivicEventCatalogLoader.AttainableMaximum). So 0.30 is 54% of everything attainable — the five live channels averaging roughly 54% coverage — and EVERY district being below that means a city that has built housing and nothing else. That happens in a rushed early game or after a reckless expansion and essentially never in a settled city: once per save at most. I considered dropping to 0.22 once the ceiling was known, and rejected it: 40% of attainable across every district is rare enough that the event would risk never firing at all, which is the failure mode the hittability rule exists to prevent. Held at 0.30, which is also glob-clinic-queues' threshold, so the two form a legible pair — that one needs one district below the line, this one needs all of them. Trigger and check are exact complements; an earlier draft checked 0.35, an unstated extra bar on top of an already brutal ask. Priced mandatory because a city in this state has no other story worth telling.
events.name: A City With Nothing In It
events.description: Not one district in the city has services worth the name. There is housing, there are roads, and past that residents are on their own everywhere they go. The figures have been the same for long enough that nobody bothers to circulate them.
events.ignoreText: Keep building housing and let the services follow the tax base. The city cannot afford both at once.
events.goalText: Get every district in the city up over the coverage line before the review.
events.powerOverrideText: Order the building programme regardless of what it costs and present the bill as settled policy.
events.successText: Every district is over the line now. The hospitals are working properly and the city feels governed for the first time.
events.failText: Nothing was built. Untreated illness and unanswered crime are now simply what living here means, and the administration owns it.

events.notes: CONFIRMED AGAINST THE REAL RANGE, and unchanged. pollution is the unweighted mean of four channels with water hard-zeroed — it is not measurable from the CPU in this pass — so it tops out at 0.75, not 1.0 (CivicEventCatalogLoader.AttainableMaximum). This threshold was set with the depressed mean already in mind and the published ceiling bears that out: 0.12 is 16% of attainable, meaning the three live channels average about 0.16, which is noticeable pollution over a wide area rather than one dirty corner. Expect it a few times in an industrial city and rarely in a service one. Exact complements: getting back under the advisory line is the ask.
events.name: Air Quality Alert
events.description: The city-wide readings have crossed the line at which the health service starts issuing advice, and the advice has been issued. Schools are keeping children indoors and the advisory has been picked up well beyond the city.
events.ignoreText: Publish the advisory, say the readings are within tolerance elsewhere, and wait for the wind to change.
events.goalText: Get the city-wide readings back below the advisory line before the next review.
events.powerOverrideText: Order the dirtiest operations to stand down and let the compensation claims arrive.
events.successText: The air has cleared, the advisory is withdrawn, and the city is a more attractive prospect than it was under the haze.
events.failText: The alert became the normal condition. The health effects are in the figures and the city is known for its air.

events.notes: Fourteen per cent out of work in a single district is common after an industrial estate closes or where housing was built far from any jobs, so expect it every few years in most saves. Trigger and check are exact complements at 0.14; an earlier draft checked 0.12, which would have failed the player over a district sitting in the 0.12-0.14 band that the story never named.
events.name: The District That Stopped Working
events.description: One part of the city has an unemployment rate the rest would call a crisis, and it has stopped making the news. The jobs that used to be within walking distance are not there any more, and neither is anything that replaced them.
events.ignoreText: The labour market will reallocate. Propping up one district's employment distorts the whole city's.
events.goalText: Get people back to work there, and leave no district above the line at the review.
events.powerOverrideText: Direct the placements and the relief where you decide they are needed and skip the process.
events.successText: People are working again. Offices are running better and local commerce has been given the room to hire.
events.failText: The district stayed idle. Long-term worklessness has settled in and the crime figures have moved with it.

events.notes: PROVISIONAL THRESHOLDS, pending the AGORA-STATCOLLECTION census. movedAwayUnhappy is census-gated, so it is authored as a delta, and BOTH HALVES NOW ASSUME ONE READING: cumulative since founding, under which the trigger means a hundred and fifty people leaving unhappy in half a year — a running rate of about twenty-five a month — and the check means fewer than seventeen over the one month the story lives, so roughly two thirds of the rate that opened it. An earlier draft checked 'delta <= 0', which under the same reading demanded that nobody at all leave unhappy, so failText printed at every resolution. RE-DERIVED FOR THE ONE-MONTH STORY LIFE: the draft after that asked for fewer than thirty-five over two months, the same rate measured over a span the player did not own. The reading is not statically resolvable: m_CollectionType is authored asset data on StatisticsPrefab/StatisticsData and refsrc holds decompiled C# only, which is why wave 1 specified a runtime census. Set below glob-population-exodus deliberately, because unhappy departures are a subset of all departures.
events.name: They Were Asked Why
events.description: The exit figures now come with a reason attached, and for half a year the reason has been the city itself. It is a small number against the population and a very large one against the administration's account of how things are going.
events.ignoreText: Every city loses the people it does not suit. Dwelling on the reasons will not bring any of them back.
events.goalText: Slow the unhappy departures to a trickle before the next review.
events.powerOverrideText: Discontinue the question on the form and let the series end with it.
events.successText: The unhappy departures have slowed right down. There is more in the city worth staying for and it shows in the parks.
events.failText: More left, and for the same reason. The city's reputation has caught up with its figures and both are working against it.
